messages:
kevin (product): Thanks all 12 dropping a short thread for the pricing/usage follow-ups from today's all-hands. Keep Qs bite-sized and we'll answer quickly.
tess (eng): Quick Q: are promo/marketing credits treated as part of the monthly quota or as a separate bucket? Customers are asking.
sam (finance): Promo credits are separate until consumed. They do not decrement committed monthly quota counts; they just reduce billable usage while available. We show them as a distinct line on invoices.
maya (support): If a long-running streaming job runs out of credits mid-stream, what's the signal we send? 402 or 429? What should SDKs expect?
dmitri (ops): Short: 402 (Payment Required) for terminal credit exhaustion. 429 for rate-limit throttles. For streams we try to finish a safe checkpoint, then emit a final 402 payload/footer when feasible.
tess (eng): Thanks. Related: when we fallback from a larger model to a smaller one under load, which model's price is charged? And do we bill any orchestration/assembly work?
sam (finance): We bill the model that actually served the tokens. Orchestration/assembly work that consumes tokens/time is billed as separate line items (labeled in the usage CSV as server-side ops). Customers get a breakdown in the usage export so they can reconcile.
maya (support): Is there a self-serve control for customers to hard-block expensive routes (to prevent runaway tests)?
dmitri (ops): Yes 12 Console -> Quotas lets org admins set hard blocks per-route and per-project. There's also a Quotas API (POST /v1/orgs/{org}/quotas). Use `safety: true` in the rule to create a safety-hold that requires ops review.
quota-bot: FYI: "Trial alert thresholds at 50/75/90% enabled by default for newly created trials."
kevin (product): Policy Q: refunds vs credits 12 what's the typical path? Customers want to know if we refund to card or issue invoice credits.
sam (finance): Standard practice: issue a credit memo applied to the next invoice for most cases. Refund to card is rare and handled case-by-case (large disputes, regulatory reasons). If >$10k or legal requirement, finance escalates to payment ops.
tess (eng): One more operational: can we programmatically request a temporary trial-topup to finish a POC (like a one-off bump)?
sam (finance): We can approve small one-off top-ups for POCs; larger bumps require a short SOW. Email finance@redwood.ai with org id, desired amount, and justification. We aim to respond within 2 business days.
maya (support): Perfect. I'll gather these answers into a short FAQ draft and ping back for review. :white_check_mark:
